item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Israel Strikes Tehran After Pakistan Offers to Host U.S.-Iran Talks
item.summary: The Pentagon said it was sending 2,000 airborne troops to the Middle East, even as President Trump seemed to endorse Pakistan’s offer to broker negotiations. It was unclear whether Iran and Israel supported a U.S. peace plan.

item.title: Cheap Drones Remain Wild Card in Iran war
item.summary: Stopping Iran’s production of drones is critical to opening the Strait of Hormuz and halting its attacks on Gulf nations. But can it be done?

item.title: Investigators Seek Answers in Attacks on Jewish Sites in Europe
item.summary: Attacks on schools and property in several countries have Jewish communities on edge, amid suspicions that Iran is behind the violence.

item.title: Here’s What Happened in the War in the Middle East on Tuesday
item.summary: The U.S. was said to have sent Iran a peace plan via Pakistan on a day that the Iranians fired a torrent of missiles across the region.

item.title: Iran Signals Resilience With Volley of Missiles Across Middle East
item.summary: The barrage continued as officials said the U.S. had sent Iran a 15-point plan to end the war. But Iranian officials have publicly denied that Washington and Tehran are talking directly.

item.title: Plan to Disarm Hamas in Gaza Is Detailed at U.N.
item.summary: A Board of Peace member said the most dangerous weapons would be collected first. He linked compliance with disarmament to reconstruction beginning in the enclave.

item.title: Ukraine Finally Got Battlefield Momentum. Now Comes a Russian Offensive.
item.summary: Moscow’s forces are intensifying their attacks in southern Ukraine after Kyiv made rare gains along the front.

item.title: The U.S. Military Said It Helped Bomb a Drug Camp in Ecuador. It Was a Dairy Farm.
item.summary: The Times visited a village where the United States and Ecuador said they destroyed an armed group’s training camp. Residents said it was actually a dairy farm.

item.title: Iran Says ‘Non-Hostile’ Ships Can Sail Through the Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: Ships with no ties to Israel or the United States would be allowed to pass, the government said, but it was unclear if any vessels would try.

item.title: An American in Russia Is Linked to Neo-Nazi Terror Cells Across Europe
item.summary: F.B.I. agents thought they had weakened an online hate group known as the Base. A string of European terrorism cases indicates it has resurged.
